body_markdown:
A self-storage unit helps community groups organize reusable event supplies, speed up setup and cleanup, and clear space between fundraisers, volunteer projects, and annual gatherings.


**The Basics**


- Since community events are often a group effort, organization is key.


- Create one central storage system for reusable community-event supplies.


- Create an inventory and checkout list so organizers know what supplies are in storage, what needs replacement, and who has taken items for an upcoming event.


- A clear layout helps everyone get in and get out fast.


- Sort supplies by event type, project, volunteer team, or setup area.


- Pack supplies in event-day order: store items needed first near the front of the unit, and load those items last so the setup crew reaches them first.


- Community groups usually have low budgets, so take good care of the items that need to last.


- Choose the right unit for your group’s needs.


- Choose Drive-Up Access when volunteers need to pull a vehicle directly up to a ground-level unit to make loading easier and frequent visits more convenient.


- Consider 24/7 Access at select locations when setup starts early, cleanup ends late, or volunteers need to work around changing schedules.


- Use Public Storage’s month-to-month rental agreements to keep event supplies organized during a fundraiser season, annual event schedule, or time-limited volunteer project.


## Create One Central Event-Supply System


**Creating one central event-supply system gives organizers and volunteers a consistent place to find, return, and track reusable materials.** Instead of asking several people to store tables, signs, bins, and décor at home, designate one self-storage unit as the group’s supply hub. All involved will be relieved that a shared space is a resource for them to reduce the clutter in their own homes.


Use the unit for items such as:


- Folding tables and chairs


- Banners, signs, and display stands


- Non-perishable collection containers


- Auction items and display materials


- Decorations and seasonal event supplies


- Children’s activity materials


- Tablecloths, empty serving pieces, and setup supplies


- Volunteer shirts, name tags, and event materials


Keep food, beverages, perishables, wet items, live plants, cleaners, fuel, propane, and other restricted materials out of the unit.


## Organize Supplies Logically


**Organizing supplies by event and setup area helps volunteers load the right materials and begin setup without searching through unrelated bins.** Create defined sections for each recurring event, project, or team.


**Event Area & Supply Type**


**Organization Method**


Registration & Check-In


Group signs, name tags, table covers, pens, and empty collection containers


Auction & Fundraiser Displays


Store display stands, bid-signage materials, décor, and table supplies together


Children’s Activities & Games


Pack reusable activity materials in labeled bins by project or age group


Volunteer Projects & Cleanup


Group gloves, approved tools, signs, bins, and non-hazardous supplies by project


Seasonal Events & Décor


Label bins by holiday, season, or annual event


Folding Tables & Chairs


Store larger pieces along unit walls for easier loading


Use clear labels that identify the event, contents, and setup area. For example, label a container “Spring Fun Run — Registration Table,” rather than simply “Event Supplies.”


Beyond general layout,


**packing supplies in event-day order helps the setup team unload and arrange materials efficiently.** Store items needed first near the front of the unit, then load those items last into the vehicle so they come out first at the event site.


For a fundraiser, that order might look like:


1. Registration signs, tables, and check-in supplies


1. Directional signage and display stands


1. Activity, auction, or volunteer-project materials


1. Extra décor and backup supplies


1. Cleanup bins and return labels


After the event, reverse the process. Count supplies, clean and dry reusable items, and return each bin to its designated section. This reset prepares the group for the next event instead of creating a larger organizing job later.


## Build an Inventory & Checkout Process


**Building an inventory and checkout process helps organizers track shared supplies and identify what needs replacement before the next event.** A simple shared spreadsheet, document, or note on your phone or even a paper binder that lives in the space would work well.


Include these details:


- Item name and quantity


- Bin or shelf location


- Event or team that uses the item


- Volunteer who checked it out


- Pickup date and return date


- Condition notes


- Supplies that need replacement or replenishment


Assign one event lead to update the list after each pickup and return. This process helps groups avoid duplicate purchases and keeps event budgets focused on current needs.


## Choose a Unit That Fits Your Group


**Choosing a self-storage unit that fits your group’s needs starts with getting an idea of what will need to be stored.** After measuring the large items like folding tables, chairs, signs, and other bigger items, count bins and boxes and consider whether your team needs to add extra room for shelving, an access aisle, or frequent seasonal rotations


.


**Unit Size & Group Storage Needs**


**Typical Fit**


**5′ x 5′**


Bins of signage, décor, registration materials, and smaller event supplies


**5′ x 10′**


Multiple bins, folding chairs, tablecloths, display materials, and smaller furniture


**10′ x 10′**


Folding tables, chairs, seasonal supplies, banners, and materials for recurring events


**10′ x 15′ or Larger**


Larger equipment, extensive event décor, multiple tables, and supplies for several teams


Community groups often work with limited budgets, so choose a unit that fits your inventory without paying for unused space. Use the


[Public Storage Size Guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) to find the right size for your group, then search for the Public Storage location closest to your event location, close to your meeting space, or in a central location convenient to all volunteers. With more than 4,600 facilities in the US


, a location won’t be far away


.


****


## Match Storage Features to Your Needs


**Matching storage features to your event team’s needs and schedules to help volunteers retrieve supplies with less time and effort.**


Choose


**Drive-Up Access** when your team needs to pull a vehicle directly up to their ground-level unit. Your team could use this feature to reduce carrying distance for supplies, address a volunteer’s mobility issues, or simply make frequent visits to the space faster.


Choose


**24/7 Access, a feature that allows renters to visit their unit anytime they need, day or night.** This feature is key when volunteers need supplies before an early setup before or a late cleanup after an event. Public Storage offers 24/7 Access at more than 2,400 of its facilities, though availability and enrollment requirements vary by location. If 24/7 Access is not available at the location you choose, extended gate access hours may be available.


All Public Storage facilities also boast features such as electronic gate access, video surveillance, perimeter fencing, on-site management, dedicated Loss Prevention professionals, and a 24/7 Security Operations Center. Staff also perform regular property checks, routine common-area cleaning, and ongoing pest-control efforts to ensure facilities are well kept.


Public Storage operates more than 4,600 facilities across 42 states, making it easier to search for a location near an event venue, in a central location convenient to all volunteers, or close to the organizer’s home.


## Keep Your Rental Flexible


**Month-to-month self-storage lets community groups match storage to an event calendar instead of committing to a long-term agreement.** Reserve a unit for a fundraising season, a neighborhood event series, or a time-limited volunteer project, then adjust your plans when and if the schedule changes.


Public Storage rentals are all leased as month-to-month agreements, and customers can complete a rental online in minutes with no credit card required. Search


[Public Storage locations](https://www.publicstorage.com/find-storage) to compare nearby facilities, unit sizes, features, and availability.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**How Can I Organize Supplies for My Community Event?**


You can organize supplies for your community event by sorting materials by event, volunteer team, or setup area; labeling every bin; and creating a central inventory list. Keep the next event’s supplies near the front of the unit for faster pickup.


**What Should I Store for a Fundraiser or Volunteer Project?**


You should store clean, dry, non-perishable fundraiser or volunteer-project supplies, such as folding tables, chairs, banners, signs, décor, display materials, and empty collection containers. Keep food, beverages, perishables, wet items, live plants, and hazardous materials out of the unit.


**Do I Need Drive-Up Access for Community Event Supplies?**


You should choose Drive-Up Access for community event supplies when volunteers need to move large or bulky items or have to make frequent trips to the unit. Drive-Up Access lets you pull your vehicle directly up to select ground-level units, reducing the distance you carry event materials and time spent on-site.


**Can My Volunteer Team Access Storage Outside Standard Hours?**


You can access storage outside standard hours at select Public Storage locations that offer 24/7 Access. This option helps teams preparing for early events or completing late cleanup. Check the


[Public Storage location finder](https://www.publicstorage.com/find-storage) for local availability.


**Can My Team Rent Storage Only During Fundraiser Season?**


You can rent storage only during fundraiser season through Public Storage’s month-to-month rental agreements. This flexibility helps your group keep supplies organized during active event periods without a long-term rental agreement.
